record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.original_question: Determine the possible values of dim Z(X) when X is a 5-dimensional real Banach space.

evidence.quote: Problem 28. What are the possible values for the dimension of Z(X) when X is a 5-dimensional real Banach space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space and let $L(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. An operator $T \in L(X)$ is called a multiplier if every extreme point $p$ of the dual unit ball of $X$ is an eigenvector of the adjoint $T^*$, i.e., $T^*p = a_T(p)\, p$ for some scalar $a_T(p)$. The centralizer of $X$, denoted $Z(X)$, is defined as
$$Z(X) = \{T \in L(X) : T \text{ and } S \text{ are multipliers for some } S \in L(X) \text{ with } a_S = i a_T \text{ in the complex case}\},$$
or equivalently, in the real case, $Z(X)$ is the set of multipliers $T$ for which the corresponding function $a_T$ is real-valued on the extreme points of the dual unit ball; $Z(X)$ is a closed unital subalgebra of $L(X)$ which is isometrically isomorphic, as a real Banach algebra, to $C_{\mathbb{R}}(K)$ for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.

Determine the set of all possible values of $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} Z(X)$ as $X$ ranges over all $5$-dimensional real Banach spaces.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not produce a definitive reference resolving the possible values of $\dim Z(X)$ for $5$-dimensional real Banach spaces. The question appears in lists of open problems on the numerical index of Banach spaces, and no subsequent paper identifying the complete set of attainable dimensions in the $5$-dimensional case was located.
